newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurobourses pick up slightly,Xmas trade thin.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurobourses pick up slightly,Xmas trade thin.

text.p: European bourses perked up slightly on Monday but trading was thin ahead of the Christmas break and some investors took profits after recent strong gains.
On currency markets, the dollar was barely changed from levels seen late on Friday and business was quiet with most dealing rooms winding down for the holiday.

The London stock exchange's blue chip FTSE index clawed back early losses to show a small profit by lunch-time, but overall, dealings were light and traders said they expected volume to taper off even further as the day progressed.
"Unless there's a bid or some big surprise, I think we're just going to drift like this," a dealer said.

Monday's modest profits in London, Europe's biggest bourse, came after the index closed at a peak of 4,077.6 on Friday, eclipsing the record set on October 21. At one point the FTSE was as high as 4,100.

No British figures were due on Monday but traders were keeping an eye open for the U.S. November personal income and spending data to be released at 1330 GMT. A U.S. survey on consumer confidence for November was due at 1500 GMT.
Frankfurt's DAX index, which had surged 1.66 percent on Friday, was down 0.4 percent and the thin trading was likely to preclude any chance of a revival of the pre-Christmas rally.
"We will be lucky if all the DAX shares have started trading by the floor opening," said one Frankfurt dealer, referring to the sluggish start of electronic dealings.
In Paris, shares slipped in and out of profit but was marginally in the plus column at midday.
Moulinex was down 3.69 percent at 117.50. The company on Friday announced it had cut its first half loss and announced plans for a 500 million franc ($95 million) capital increase.
On the currency front, the dollar was at 1.5532 marks and 114.21 yen, compared to 1.5521 and 114.20 in late European trade on Friday.

Currency traders also said they were awaiting the U.S. economic data due later, which would give clues on the health of the American economy, but were thought unlikely to have an immediate implications for interest rates.
Although the most likely scenario was for the dollar to remain at current levels in narrow ranges, any sharp moves on U.S. asset markets would have a knock-on effect, dealers said.
CURRENCIES AT 1230 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.5532 marks and 114.15 yen, compared with 1.5521 marks and 114.20 yen in late European business on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1230 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was up 5.9 points, at 4,083.4.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 0.68 at 2,279.21.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 11.11 points at 2,843.34.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $368.70 an ounce, compared to $369.35 on Friday. Silver was unhanged at $4.84.
